questions.stem: Square P has a side length of \(x\) inches. Square Q has a perimeter that is 176 inches greater than the perimeter of square P. The function \(f\) gives the area of square Q, in square inches. Which of the following defines \(f\)?
questions.explanation: Perimeter of P is \(4x\), so perimeter of Q is \(4x + 176\), and side of Q is \(\frac{4x + 176}{4} = x + 44\). The area is \(f(x) = (x + 44)^2\).

questions.stem: The expression \(4x^2 + bx - 45\), where \(b\) is a constant, can be rewritten as \((hx + k)(x + j)\), where \(h\), \(k\), and \(j\) are integer constants. Which of the following must be an integer?
questions.explanation: Expanding \((hx + k)(x + j) = hx^2 + (hj + k)x + kj\). Matching constants: \(kj = -45\), so \(\frac{45}{k} = -j\), an integer. The other quotients need not be integers.

questions.stem: In the \(xy\)-plane, a parabola has vertex \((9, -14)\) and intersects the \(x\)-axis at two points. If the equation of the parabola is written in the form \(y = ax^2 + bx + c\), where \(a\), \(b\), and \(c\) are constants, which of the following could be the value of \(a + b + c\)?
questions.explanation: In vertex form \(y = a(x - 9)^2 - 14\). Then \(a + b + c = y(1) = a(1-9)^2 - 14 = 64a - 14\). Since the parabola opens upward to cross the x-axis twice from vertex below the axis, \(a > 0\), making \(64a - 14 > -14\). Only \(-12\) exceeds \(-14\) and gives \(a = \frac{2}{64} > 0\).

questions.stem: \(-4x^2 - 7x = -36\) What is the positive solution to the given equation?
questions.explanation: Rewrite as \(4x^2 + 7x - 36 = 0\). Factoring: \((4x - 9)(x + 4) = 0\), giving \(x = \frac{9}{4}\) or \(x = -4\). The positive solution is \(\frac{9}{4}\).

questions.stem: \(f(x) = (x - 10)(x + 13)\) The function \(f\) is defined by the given equation. For what value of \(x\) does \(f(x)\) reach its minimum?
questions.explanation: The zeros are \(x = 10\) and \(x = -13\). The vertex (minimum, since parabola opens up) is at the midpoint: \(x = \frac{10 + (-13)}{2} = -\frac{3}{2}\).

questions.stem: The function \(f(x) = \frac{1}{9}(x - 7)^2 + 3\) gives a metal ball's height above the ground \(f(x)\), in inches, \(x\) seconds after it started moving on a track, where \(0 \le x \le 10\). Which of the following is the best interpretation of the vertex of the graph of \(y = f(x)\) in the \(xy\)-plane?
options: The metal ball's minimum height was 3 inches above the ground.
The metal ball's minimum height was 7 inches above the ground.
The metal ball's height was 3 inches above the ground when it started moving.
The metal ball's height was 7 inches above the ground when it started moving.
questions.explanation: The vertex is at \((7, 3)\). Since the coefficient \(\frac{1}{9}\) is positive, the vertex is a minimum, so the ball's minimum height was 3 inches above the ground.

questions.stem: A right rectangular prism has a height of 9 inches. The length of the prism's base is \(x\) inches, which is 7 inches more than the width of the prism's base. Which function \(V\) gives the volume of the prism, in cubic inches, in terms of the length of the prism's base?
questions.explanation: The length is \(x\), the width is \(x - 7\), and the height is 9. Volume \(= \text{length} \times \text{width} \times \text{height} = 9x(x - 7)\).

questions.stem: The function \(f\) is defined by \(f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c\), where \(a\), \(b\), and \(c\) are constants. The graph of \(y = f(x)\) in the \(xy\)-plane passes through the points \((7, 0)\) and \((-3, 0)\). If \(a\) is an integer greater than 1, which of the following could be the value of \(a + b\)?
questions.explanation: With roots 7 and \(-3\), \(f(x) = a(x - 7)(x + 3) = a(x^2 - 4x - 21)\), so \(b = -4a\) and \(a + b = a - 4a = -3a\). For integer \(a > 1\): \(a = 2\) gives \(-6\). So \(-6\) is possible.

questions.stem: Which expression is equivalent to \(16x^3 y^2 + 14xy\)?
questions.explanation: The greatest common factor of \(16x^3 y^2\) and \(14xy\) is \(2xy\). Factoring: \(2xy(8x^2 y + 7)\), since \(2xy \cdot 8x^2 y = 16x^3 y^2\) and \(2xy \cdot 7 = 14xy\).

questions.stem: The kinetic energy, in joules, of an object with mass 9 kilograms traveling at a speed of \(v\) meters per second is given by the function \(K\), where \(K(v) = \frac{9}{2}v^2\). Which of the following is the best interpretation of \(K(34) = 5{,}202\) in this context?
options: The object traveling at 34 meters per second has a kinetic energy of 5,202 joules.
The object traveling at 340 meters per second has a kinetic energy of 5,202 joules.
The object traveling at 5,202 meters per second has a kinetic energy of 34 joules.
The object traveling at 23,409 meters per second has a kinetic energy of 34 joules.
questions.explanation: In \(K(v)\), the input \(v = 34\) is the speed and the output 5,202 is the kinetic energy, so an object at 34 meters per second has 5,202 joules of kinetic energy.

questions.stem: Which expression is equivalent to \((8x^3 + 8) - (x^3 - 2)\)?
questions.explanation: Distribute the subtraction: \(8x^3 + 8 - x^3 + 2 = 7x^3 + 10\).

questions.stem: Which quadratic equation has no real solutions?
questions.explanation: A quadratic has no real solutions when its discriminant \(b^2 - 4ac < 0\). For \(5x^2 - 14x + 49\): \((-14)^2 - 4(5)(49) = 196 - 980 = -784 < 0\), so it has no real solutions.

questions.stem: \(k^2 - 53 = 91\) What is the positive solution to the given equation?
questions.explanation: \(k^2 = 91 + 53 = 144\), so \(k = \sqrt{144} = 12\) (positive solution).

questions.stem: Which expression is equivalent to \((x^2 + 11)^2 + (x - 5)(x + 5)\)?
\(w^2 + 12w - 40 = 0\) Which of the following is a solution to the given equation?
questions.explanation: Using the quadratic formula: \(w = \frac{-12 \pm \sqrt{144 + 160}}{2} = \frac{-12 \pm \sqrt{304}}{2} = -6 \pm 2\sqrt{19}\). One solution is \(-6 + 2\sqrt{19}\).

questions.stem: Which expression is equivalent to \(5x^5 - 6x^4 + 8x^3\)?
questions.explanation: The greatest common factor of the three terms is \(x^3\). Factoring: \(x^3(5x^2 - 6x + 8)\).

questions.stem: \((x + 2)(x - 5)(x + 9) = 0\) What is a positive solution to the given equation?
questions.explanation: Setting each factor to zero gives \(x = -2, 5, -9\). The positive solution is 5.

questions.stem: \(x^2 = -841\) How many distinct real solutions does the given equation have?
questions.explanation: A squared real number cannot be negative, so \(x^2 = -841\) has no real solutions: zero.

questions.stem: Which expression is equivalent to \(23x^3 + 2x^2 + 9x\)?
questions.explanation: The greatest common factor is \(x\). Factoring: \(x(23x^2 + 2x + 9)\).

questions.stem: Which expression is equivalent to \((9x^3 + 5x + 7) + (6x^3 + 5x^2 - 5)\)?

\(h(t) = -16t^2 + b\) The function \(h\) estimates an object's height, in feet, above the ground \(t\) seconds after the object is dropped, where \(b\) is a constant. The function estimates that the object is 3,364 feet above the ground when it is dropped at \(t = 0\). Approximately how many seconds after being dropped does the function estimate the object will hit the ground?
questions.explanation: At \(t = 0\), \(h = b = 3{,}364\). The object hits the ground when \(h = 0\): \(-16t^2 + 3{,}364 = 0 \Rightarrow t^2 = 210.25 \Rightarrow t = 14.5\) seconds.

questions.stem: \(x - 29 = (x - a)(x - 29)\) Which of the following are solutions to the given equation, where \(a\) is a constant and \(a > 30\)? I. \(a\) II. \(a + 1\) III. \(29\)
questions.explanation: Rewrite as \((x - 29) - (x - a)(x - 29) = 0\), so \((x - 29)[1 - (x - a)] = 0\), giving \((x - 29)(a + 1 - x) = 0\). Solutions are \(x = 29\) (III) and \(x = a + 1\) (II). So II and III only.

questions.stem: In the \(xy\)-plane, the graph of the equation \(y = -x^2 + 9x - 100\) intersects the line \(y = c\) at exactly one point. What is the value of \(c\)?
questions.explanation: The line \(y = c\) touches the parabola at exactly one point when \(c\) equals the maximum value at the vertex. The vertex \(x\)-value is \(\frac{-9}{2(-1)} = \frac{9}{2}\), and \(y = -\left(\frac{9}{2}\right)^2 + 9\left(\frac{9}{2}\right) - 100 = -\frac{81}{4} + \frac{81}{2} - 100 = \frac{81}{4} - 100 = -\frac{319}{4}\).

questions.stem: The function \(f\) is defined by \(f(x) = 7x^3\). In the \(xy\)-plane, the graph of \(y = g(x)\) is the result of shifting the graph of \(y = f(x)\) down 2 units. Which equation defines function \(g\)?
questions.explanation: Shifting down 2 units subtracts 2 from the output: \(g(x) = 7x^3 - 2\).

questions.stem: \(\frac{x^2}{\sqrt{x^2 - c^2}} = \frac{c^2}{\sqrt{x^2 - c^2}} + 39\) In the given equation, \(c\) is a positive constant. Which of the following is one of the solutions to the given equation?
questions.explanation: Multiply through: \(\frac{x^2 - c^2}{\sqrt{x^2 - c^2}} = 39\), so \(\sqrt{x^2 - c^2} = 39\). Squaring gives \(x^2 - c^2 = 39^2\), so \(x^2 = c^2 + 39^2\) and \(x = \pm\sqrt{c^2 + 39^2}\). One solution is \(-\sqrt{c^2 + 39^2}\).

questions.stem: The function \(g\) is defined by \(g(x) = x^2 + 9\). For which value of \(x\) is \(g(x) = 25\)?
questions.explanation: Set \(x^2 + 9 = 25\), so \(x^2 = 16\) and \(x = 4\) (a valid choice).

questions.stem: Function \(f\) is defined by \(f(x) = (x + 6)(x + 5)(x + 1)\). Function \(g\) is defined by \(g(x) = f(x - 1)\). The graph of \(y = g(x)\) in the \(xy\)-plane has \(x\)-intercepts at \((a, 0)\), \((b, 0)\), and \((c, 0)\), where \(a\), \(b\), and \(c\) are distinct constants. What is the value of \(a + b + c\)?
questions.explanation: The roots of \(f\) are \(-6, -5, -1\). Since \(g(x) = f(x - 1)\), the graph shifts right 1 unit, so the roots become \(-5, -4, 0\). Their sum is \(-5 + (-4) + 0 = -9\).

questions.stem: \(f(x) = 4x^2 + 64x + 262\) The function \(g\) is defined by \(g(x) = f(x + 5)\). For what value of \(x\) does \(g(x)\) reach its minimum?
questions.explanation: The minimum of \(f\) is at \(x = \frac{-64}{2(4)} = -8\). Since \(g(x) = f(x + 5)\), the graph shifts left 5 units, so its minimum is at \(x = -8 - 5 = -13\).

questions.stem: \(x + 7 = 10\), \((x + 7)^2 = y\) Which ordered pair \((x, y)\) is a solution to the given system of equations?
\(y = 76\), \(y = x^2 - 5\) The graphs of the given equations in the \(xy\)-plane intersect at the point \((x, y)\). What is a possible value of \(x\)?
questions.explanation: Set \(x^2 - 5 = 76\), so \(x^2 = 81\) and \(x = \pm 9\). A possible value is \(-9\).

questions.stem: \(|-5x + 13| = 73\) What is the sum of the solutions to the given equation?
\(-9x^2 + 30x + c = 0\) In the given equation, \(c\) is a constant. The equation has exactly one solution. What is the value of \(c\)?
questions.explanation: A quadratic has exactly one solution when its discriminant is 0: \(30^2 - 4(-9)(c) = 900 + 36c = 0\), so \(c = -25\).

questions.stem: Which of the following expressions has a factor of \(x + 2b\), where \(b\) is a positive integer constant?
questions.explanation: If \(x + 2b\) is a factor, then \(3x^2 + Bx + 14b = (x + 2b)(3x + 7)\) for the constant term to match (\(2b \cdot 7 = 14b\)). Expanding: \((x + 2b)(3x + 7) = 3x^2 + (7 + 6b)x + 14b\). Matching the middle coefficient to \(49\): \(7 + 6b = 49 \Rightarrow b = 7\), an integer. So \(3x^2 + 49x + 14b\) has the factor.

questions.stem: \(8x^2 - 40 = 32\) What is the positive solution to the given equation?
questions.explanation: Add 40 to both sides: \(8x^2 = 72\), so \(x^2 = 9\) and the positive solution is \(x = 3\).

questions.stem: Which quadratic equation has exactly one distinct real solution?
questions.explanation: \((x + 15)^2 = 0\) gives the single repeated solution \(x = -15\). A negative right side (option B) has no real solution, and a positive right side (options C and D) yields two distinct solutions.

questions.stem: A table shows three values of \(x\) and their corresponding values of \(f(x)\) for the quadratic function \(f\): when \(x = 24\), \(f(x) = -8\); when \(x = 30\), \(f(x) = -8\); when \(x = 32\), \(f(x) = 8\). Which equation defines \(f\)?
questions.explanation: Since \(f(24) = f(30) = -8\), test \(f(x) = (x - 24)(x - 30) - 8\): at \(x = 24\) and \(x = 30\) the product is 0, giving \(-8\); at \(x = 32\), \((8)(2) - 8 = 16 - 8 = 8\). All three values match.

questions.stem: \(f(x) = -6x^2 + 60x - 126\) The function \(f\) is defined by the given equation. Which of the following equivalent forms of the equation displays the maximum value of the function as a constant or coefficient?
questions.explanation: The vertex form \(f(x) = -6(x - 5)^2 + 24\) shows the maximum value 24 as a constant (the parabola opens downward, so the vertex is a maximum).

questions.stem: \(52(x^3 + 64)(x^4 - 81) = 0\) How many distinct real solutions does the given equation have?
questions.explanation: The factor \(x^3 + 64 = 0\) gives one real solution, \(x = -4\). The factor \(x^4 - 81 = 0\) gives \(x^4 = 81\), with two real solutions \(x = 3\) and \(x = -3\) (the other two roots are non-real). In total there are 3 distinct real solutions.

questions.stem: What are the solutions to \(x^2 - 5x + 6 = 0\)?
questions.explanation: Factor: \(x^2 - 5x + 6 = (x - 2)(x - 3)\). Setting each factor to zero gives \(x = 2\) and \(x = 3\).

questions.stem: What are the solutions to \(x^2 - 5x + 4 = 0\)?
questions.explanation: Factor: \(x^2 - 5x + 4 = (x - 1)(x - 4)\). Setting each factor to zero gives \(x = 1\) and \(x = 4\).

questions.stem: What are the solutions to \(x^2 - 8x + 15 = 0\)?
questions.explanation: Factor: \(x^2 - 8x + 15 = (x - 3)(x - 5)\). Setting each factor to zero gives \(x = 3\) and \(x = 5\).

questions.stem: What are the solutions to \(x^2 - 8x + 12 = 0\)?
questions.explanation: Factor: \(x^2 - 8x + 12 = (x - 2)(x - 6)\). Setting each factor to zero gives \(x = 2\) and \(x = 6\).

questions.stem: What are the solutions to \(x^2 - 8x + 7 = 0\)?
questions.explanation: Factor: \(x^2 - 8x + 7 = (x - 1)(x - 7)\). Setting each factor to zero gives \(x = 1\) and \(x = 7\).

questions.stem: What are the solutions to \(x^2 - 9x + 20 = 0\)?
questions.explanation: Factor: \(x^2 - 9x + 20 = (x - 4)(x - 5)\). Setting each factor to zero gives \(x = 4\) and \(x = 5\).

questions.stem: What are the solutions to \(x^2 - 6x + 8 = 0\)?
questions.explanation: Factor: \(x^2 - 6x + 8 = (x - 2)(x - 4)\). Setting each factor to zero gives \(x = 2\) and \(x = 4\).

questions.stem: What are the solutions to \(x^2 + 5x + 6 = 0\)?
questions.explanation: Factor: \(x^2 + 5x + 6 = (x - -2)(x - -3)\). Setting each factor to zero gives \(x = -2\) and \(x = -3\).

questions.stem: What are the solutions to \(x^2 + 6x + 5 = 0\)?
questions.explanation: Factor: \(x^2 + 6x + 5 = (x - -1)(x - -5)\). Setting each factor to zero gives \(x = -1\) and \(x = -5\).

questions.stem: What are the solutions to \(x^2 - 7x + 12 = 0\)?
questions.explanation: Factor: \(x^2 - 7x + 12 = (x - 3)(x - 4)\). Setting each factor to zero gives \(x = 3\) and \(x = 4\).

questions.stem: What are the solutions to \(x^2 - 3x - 10 = 0\)?
questions.explanation: Factor: \(x^2 - 3x - 10 = (x - -2)(x - 5)\). Setting each factor to zero gives \(x = -2\) and \(x = 5\).

questions.stem: What are the solutions to \(x^2 - 7x + 6 = 0\)?
questions.explanation: Factor: \(x^2 - 7x + 6 = (x - 1)(x - 6)\). Setting each factor to zero gives \(x = 1\) and \(x = 6\).

questions.stem: What are the solutions to \(x^2 + x - 6 = 0\)?
questions.explanation: Factor: \(x^2 + x - 6 = (x - -3)(x - 2)\). Setting each factor to zero gives \(x = -3\) and \(x = 2\).

questions.stem: What are the solutions to \(x^2 - 11x + 30 = 0\)?
questions.explanation: Factor: \(x^2 - 11x + 30 = (x - 5)(x - 6)\). Setting each factor to zero gives \(x = 5\) and \(x = 6\).

questions.stem: Factor completely: \(x^2 - 9\).
questions.explanation: This is a difference of squares: \(x^2 - 9 = (x - 3)(x + 3)\).

questions.stem: What is the constant term of \((x - 4)(x + 6)\)?
questions.explanation: The constant is the product of the constants: \((-4)(6) = -24\).

questions.stem: One solution of \(x^2 - 7x + 12 = 0\) is \(x = 3\). What is the other solution?
questions.explanation: The roots multiply to \(12\): \(3 \cdot r = 12\), so \(r = 4\).

questions.stem: What is the \(y\)-intercept of \(y = x^2 - 2x - 8\)?
Factor: \(x^2 + 6x + 9\).
questions.explanation: This is a perfect square: \(x^2 + 6x + 9 = (x + 3)^2\).

questions.stem: For \(f(x) = x^2 + x\), what is \(f(-3)\)?
What value of \(x\) makes \(x^2 = 49\) with \(x > 0\)?
questions.explanation: \(x^2 = 49\) gives \(x = \pm 7\); the positive solution is \(7\).

questions.stem: Factor out the greatest common factor: \(6x^2 + 9x\).
The graph of \(y = (x - 2)^2 + 5\) has its vertex at which point?
questions.explanation: In vertex form \(y = (x - h)^2 + k\), the vertex is \((h, k) = (2, 5)\).

questions.stem: What is the \(x\)-coordinate of the vertex of \(y = x^2 - 6x + 5\)?
questions.explanation: The vertex is at \(x = -\tfrac{b}{2a} = -\tfrac{-6}{2} = 3\).

questions.stem: What are the solutions to \(2x^2 - 8x = 0\)?
For what value of \(k\) does \(x^2 + kx + 9 = 0\) have exactly one real solution, with \(k > 0\)?
questions.explanation: One solution means discriminant \(= 0\): \(k^2 - 36 = 0\), so \(k = 6\) (taking \(k > 0\)).

questions.stem: The product of the roots of \(x^2 - 5x + 6 = 0\) is what?
questions.explanation: For \(x^2 + bx + c\), the product of the roots is \(c = 6\).

questions.stem: What is the minimum value of \(y = x^2 - 4x + 7\)?
questions.explanation: The vertex is at \(x = 2\); \(y = 4 - 8 + 7 = 3\), the minimum.

questions.stem: Write \(x^2 + 8x + 10\) in vertex form.
questions.explanation: Complete the square: \(x^2 + 8x + 16 - 16 + 10 = (x + 4)^2 - 6\).

questions.stem: How many real solutions does \(x^2 + 2x + 5 = 0\) have?
questions.explanation: The discriminant is \(2^2 - 4(1)(5) = -16 < 0\), so there are no real solutions.

questions.stem: If \((x - 3)\) is a factor of \(x^2 - x - 6\), what is the other factor?
questions.explanation: \(x^2 - x - 6 = (x - 3)(x + 2)\), so the other factor is \(x + 2\).

questions.stem: A ball's height is \(h(t) = -16t^2 + 32t\). At what time \(t > 0\) does it return to the ground?
The solutions of \(x^2 + bx + 12 = 0\) are \(x = 2\) and \(x = 6\). What is \(b\)?
questions.explanation: The sum of the roots is \(-b\): \(2 + 6 = 8\), so \(-b = 8\) and \(b = -8\).
Rearrange: \(x^2 - 6x + 9 = 0\), so \((x - 3)^2 = 0\) and \(x = 3\) (a double root).

questions.stem: The parabola \(y = x^2 - 2x - 3\) crosses the \(x\)-axis at which two points?
